title: Bhagavad Gita Helped Manu Bhaker Win an Olympic Medal? Survivorship Bias Explained
description:
When Manu Bhaker won a bronze at the Olympics, she credited the Bhagavad Gita for helping her stay calm under pressure. Immediately, the media and saffron brigade erupted: “See, the Gita wins medals!” But does it really?

In this video, Pale Blue Thoughts unpacks the obsession with the Bhagavad Gita and Indian athletes. From Manu Bhaker to Neeraj Chopra, athletes may draw personal inspiration from verses like “Karmanye Vadhikaraste Ma Phaleshou Kada Chana” — focus on your actions, not the fruits. That’s fine as a personal mantra. But when propaganda machines twist it into “proof” of divine power, it’s time to call out the nonsense,

We introduce the concept of survivorship bias: for every athlete quoting the Gita after success, there are countless others who prayed, read scriptures, and failed. Nobody headlines their defeats as “Gita didn’t work.” Just like in WWII, where only the surviving planes with bullet holes were studied, we’re only seeing the survivors — not the failures.

If you’ve searched for Bhagavad Gita Olympics, Manu Bhaker medal Gita, survivorship bias explained, Neeraj Chopra Gita inspiration, or sports psychology India, this documentary shows the rationalist view. The truth is: medals come from infrastructure, coaching, nutrition, training, and practice — not holy books.

#BhagavadGitaMyth #SurvivorshipBias #CriticalThinking #OlympicsIndia #ScienceOverSuperstition
